title: A Horizon for the Passage
premise: Hazel Yarrow, estranged from his archaeologist father Marcus after his mother's death, is summoned when Marcus's expedition up the Kestrel River goes silent. Following their trail with a reluctant guide, Sefa, Hazel discovers the team uncovered a pre-colonial passage through the range — and that a rival salvage crew will kill to claim it. As winter closes in, Hazel must choose between exposing the truth about what his father found (and what Marcus did to protect it) and saving the survivors. He crosses the range ahead of the snows carrying both the evidence and his father's dying confession, choosing truth over loyalty and finding, in Sefa, a love worth staying for.
about_author: Yara Sterling spent a decade leading river expeditions before turning to fiction, and her prose carries the mud, cold, and silence of real wilderness travel. She writes from a cabin she refuses to locate precisely, on the theory that good adventure stories need somewhere unaccounted for.

chapters.title: The Radio Goes Quiet
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Working a salvage dig he despises, Hazel receives word that his father's expedition has missed two scheduled check-ins. The emotional beat is resentment curdling into dread as he realizes no one else will go looking.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. He travels upriver by mail boat and finds the expedition's base camp ransacked — not by weather, but by people. First appearance of Sefa, the guide who was hired and then abandoned. Beat: wary alliance formed over shared anger at being discarded.

chapters.title: Signs of the Living
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. She reveals the team pushed on toward a canyon the maps call impassable, and that Marcus carried something sealed in oilcloth. Beat: Hazel's guilt deepens — his father trusted strangers with secrets he never shared with his own child.

chapters.title: The Salvage Men
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At a trading post they encounter Voss's crew, posing as a rescue party but asking the wrong questions. Hazel lies badly; Sefa covers. Beat: first taste of real danger, and the realization the race has already started without them.

chapters.title: Cold Camp
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating scenes. A freezing night forces honesty: Hazel admits he hasn't spoken to his father in six years; Sefa admits she took the guiding job to escape a debt. Beat: intimacy born of exposure, neither quite naming it yet.

chapters.title: The First Grave
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. They find the expedition's cook dead — not from exposure, but a fall that looks staged. Burial in frozen ground. Beat: grief Hazel can't afford, and the dawning certainty that someone is erasing witnesses ahead of them.

chapters.title: Cairn at the Fork
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. A trail marker in Marcus's handwriting points toward the high pass — and warns 'not the way we came.' They realize Marcus anticipated pursuit. Beat: grudging respect for the father Hazel had written off, which feels like betrayal of his mother's memory.

chapters.title: Voss Catches Up
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Voss corners them at a river crossing, offering money for the oilcloth's location. When Hazel refuses, Voss lets them go — a message that he doesn't need to hurry. Beat: humiliation and fear; the antagonist holds every advantage but time.

chapters.title: The Passage Wall
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. They reach the canyon wall and find the ancient carved stairway — the discovery itself, half-buried, magnificent. Also find two more bodies. Beat: awe colliding with horror; wonder weaponized into a crime scene.

chapters.title: Marcus's Journal
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In a cached supply tin, Marcus's journal: he found the passage, hid the survey drawings, and refused Voss's buyers. The last entry names Hazel. Beat: the estrangement reframed — Marcus's silence was protection, which hurts worse than neglect.

chapters.title: Snowline
chapters.summary: Dual POV. First snow falls early. Sefa calculates they have four days to cross the pass or winter in the canyon with a killer behind them. Beat: love acknowledged obliquely — Sefa says she could turn back alone; Hazel realizes he no longer wants to be.

chapters.title: The Traitor Among Them
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Evidence shows one expedition member survived and is working with Voss — footprints matching boots found at the graves. Paranoia takes hold. Beat: trust between Hazel and Sefa tested by the question of who else might still be out here.

chapters.title: Ambush Below the Col
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Voss's men attack at the pass approach. Sefa is wounded; Hazel kills a man for the first time and cannot make it feel justified. Beat: the cost of survival made physical; tenderness under pressure as Hazel binds her wound.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. They capture one attacker: the expedition's surviving member, who confesses Voss promised him leniency if he delivered the drawings. Beat: Hazel confronts the theme head-on — loyalty to the dead versus truth for the living — and chooses to let the man live as witness.

chapters.title: The White Crossing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, storm sequence. Three days above the snowline, lost, half-starved, sharing body heat and finally words. Beat: the confession scene — Hazel says he loved his father even while hating him; Sefa answers with her own buried grief. Love declared in the teeth of the storm.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. They come down the far side into the valley and find Marcus alive but failing, holed up in a shepherd's hut with the oilcloth. Beat: reunion stripped of catharsis — too much damage, too little time, a father and son who don't know how to begin.

chapters.title: The Dying Confession
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Marcus tells everything: the buyers, the bribed officials, why he stayed silent even from Hazel — because knowing had gotten Hazel's mother killed years ago on an earlier dig. Beat: rage and forgiveness arriving together, unresolved, human.

chapters.title: Voss Arrives
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. Voss reaches the valley with his remaining men, demanding the drawings. Marcus, dying, tells Hazel to burn them. Beat: the climax's moral fulcrum — the truth Hazel came seeking is now his to destroy or defend.

chapters.title: Stand at the Hut
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The fight: Sefa's knowledge of the terrain turns the ground against Voss's men; Marcus takes a fatal wound buying Hazel the opening. Hazel chooses neither to burn nor surrender the drawings — he sends copies' existence public via the trading post radio. Beat: truth as the only loyalty left.

chapters.title: Ashes and Snow
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Marcus dies at dawn with Hazel's hand in his, the mountains quiet, Voss fled and exposed. Burial beside the passage he found. Beat: grief without bitterness for the first time; the wilderness forgives nothing, but Hazel forgives anyway.

chapters.title: A Horizon for the Passage
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Spring. The passage is protected as a heritage site; testimony given. Hazel and Sefa stand at the trailhead, deciding not where to go but that they'll go together. Beat: resolution — identity rebuilt not from the past uncovered but from the future chosen.
